**Question:** Should the tool check everything it can up front — that the output folder is usable and that no output file would overwrite an input file — before it writes any output file, or should it check each input as it reaches it? (FR-048, FR-049, FR-050)

**Why it matters:** This decides what the user is left holding after a failed run. Checking as it goes can leave a half-finished set of redacted files on disk before reporting a problem that was knowable before any work started; checking up front means a run either produces the whole set or touches nothing.

**Recommended:** Option B — validate the cheap, knowable-in-advance conditions (folder usable, no output/input collision across all operands) before writing anything, then stream the files. This closes the case where `--out-dir .` on the *second* of three logs has already rewritten two files, while still honouring the spec's existing decision that a genuine mid-run read or write failure leaves earlier completed files in place (FR-050).

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Check each input as it is reached — the folder is prepared on first write, and a collision or unusable folder is reported whenever it is discovered, leaving any earlier output files already written |
| B | Check the folder and every operand's output path for collisions before writing any output file; genuine read/write failures discovered later still leave earlier completed files on disk |
| C | Full all-or-nothing: validate up front *and* remove any output files already written if the run later fails, so a failing run leaves the folder as it found it |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (<=5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
